name: Varsin Matcha-Tahini Bark
description: Handpoured synth-chocolate bark swirled with ceremonial-grade matcha paste and raw tahini, broken into irregular shards and sold in wax paper packets. A genuine craft product from a Tier 2 maker space collective.
flavor_profile: Bittersweet cocoa-sub base with vegetal, umami-tinged matcha and a sesame richness from the tahini — sophisticated and slightly savory
slogan: Made in the 14th. Sold everywhere else.
cultural_context: Varsin is named for the Tier 2 maker space district where it's produced by a rotating collective of confectioners. The wax paper packaging and hand-broken shards are a deliberate anti-corporate aesthetic statement. Tier 3 consumers buy it to feel connected to something authentic; Tier 2 residents buy it because it's genuinely good and made by neighbors.
story_hooks: A major corponation has made an offer to license the Varsin name and formula — the collective is fractured over whether to accept, and a member opposed to the deal has gone to unusual lengths to sabotage negotiations.

The ceremonial matcha used in Varsin Bark comes from a single vertical farm that has just been condemned to make way for a Tier 4 development — the collective has three weeks before their supply chain disappears.

A Tier 5 food personality has anonymously declared Varsin Bark 'the best confection in GLMZ,' causing a demand surge that has overwhelmed the collective and put its artisan identity under existential pressure.
